entries.note: The commitment amount is testable, but the conclusion about underlying revenue is explicitly suggestive.
The business-weakening conclusion is qualified by 'appears' and an explicitly inexact calculation.
He suggests low customer payments rather than firmly asserting measured rates.

entries.test: CoreWeave's 2025 financial statements and contemporaneous 2026 capital expenditure guidance would establish its operating losses, spending, and expected spending increase.
entries.note: 'Time bomb' is rhetorical framing around concrete financial assertions; the 2026 figure reports an existing expectation.

entries.test: CoreWeave's FY2024 and FY2025 financial statements would establish whether its operating margin fell from approximately 17% to negative 1%.
entries.note: The proposition omits 'without debt,' which identifies the relevant margin basis. He does not firmly predict that margins will never improve.
He questions the value of the revenue and backlog, not whether those reported amounts exist. 'Fundamental weakness' supplies no shared decisive financial test.
He says it is reasonable to ask whether this might be true; he does not assert the proposed outcome.

entries.test: Hyperscalers' public financial disclosures through publication would show whether any separately disclosed revenue from renting GPUs or their own silicon.
entries.note: The proposition drops the explicit inclusion of hyperscalers' own silicon. The inference about business health is less definite than the disclosure claim.

entries.test: Publicly released financial records or corroborated reporting on OpenAI's January–September 2025 revenue and inference expenditure would settle the amounts.
entries.note: His attribution to his own reporting does not weaken the factual commitment.

entries.test: Independent demonstrations of whether AI coding tools can autonomously reproduce a functioning SaaS service, including its operational requirements, would test the claimed limitation.
entries.note: The proposition presents the broader requirements of software as the reason automatic SaaS cloning fails.

entries.test: Claude Code revenue disclosures and documented service costs would establish the $203 million revenue figure, $2.5 billion annualized rate, and claimed periods of $8–$13.50 spending per dollar earned.
entries.note: The spending ratio concerns Claude Code and applies 'at times,' not to all Anthropic revenue.

entries.test: OpenAI's completed 2025 financing rounds and Amazon's 2002–2017 capital expenditure statements would establish the nominal comparison.
entries.note: The comparison holds to the preceding nominal total, not the inflation-adjusted total also supplied.

entries.test: The round's signed financing terms, closing records, and payment disclosures as of March 3, 2026 would establish how much was funded versus conditional or payable later.
entries.note: 'Amazon put in' implies completed payment, while he subsequently says evidence suggests nobody has sent money.
He explicitly frames nonpayment as what the evidence suggests, not an established fact.
'Looting' is sarcastic condemnation. The proposition turns a reported possible share sale into an ongoing sale.

entries.test: Financial records, customer transactions, and any relevant fraud findings would establish whether these businesses earn genuine customer revenue or operate Ponzi schemes.
entries.note: He explicitly distinguishes this assertion from his preceding Ponzi-scheme joke.

entries.test: Published or subsequently disclosed business plans would show whether OpenAI and its peers have economic strategies beyond increasing revenue.
entries.note: This is a firm claim about business plans that documents could reveal, rather than an inaccessible feeling.

entries.test: OpenAI's cumulative cash burn through 2030, if it attains the referenced revenue projections, would show whether doing so required substantially more than $230 billion.
entries.note: The normalized proposition removes 'I think.' The spending requirement depends on achieving the referenced revenue trajectory.

entries.test: A public investigation, documentary disclosure, or admission establishing that sources knowingly misrepresented OpenAI's burn rate to multiple outlets would fulfill the prediction.
entries.note: The proposition drops 'I think,' although the original still expresses an affirmative future expectation.

entries.test: Recalculating the stated first-half cost ratios against the assumed second-half revenue would establish whether his conditional estimates follow.
entries.note: This is a conditional historical calculation, not a future forecast or an unconditional claim about actual expenditure.
'Than we thought' is not identical to 'than has been reported.' He offers a case for a possibility rather than a firm cost estimate.

entries.test: The stated assumptions and arithmetic, compared with publicly disclosed second-half 2025 expenditure and year-end cash, would test his estimates.
entries.note: The proposition appropriately preserves the estimates' status rather than presenting them as reported accounts.

entries.test: A reconciliation of OpenAI's starting cash, financing receipts, revenue, expenses, and cash flows would establish whether the reported loss and year-end cash are compatible.
entries.note: The proposition substitutes loss for cash burn and removes the expressly assumed starting figures.
'Far more likely' explicitly makes this a probabilistic estimate.
The proposition removes 'another possible answer' and 'I think.' It also includes an explicit explanation of why OpenAI allegedly lies.

entries.test: OpenAI's public representations and records of SoftBank's actual 2025 agent purchases would establish whether the promised $3 billion spending occurred and whether the representations were misleading.
entries.note: The source alleges an attempt to misinform; the proposition states successful misinformation more categorically.

entries.test: A dated comparison of company-sourced financial leaks with subsequently established accounts would show whether the leaks increasingly obscured the companies' finances over the preceding two years.
entries.note: The surrounding discussion supplies a concrete financial subject for 'the truth.'
The numerical discrepancies are testable, but the proposed explanation depends on the companies' private confidence about media behavior.

entries.test: Contemporaneous cost and revenue projections compared with actual results for OpenAI and Anthropic would establish the claimed pattern of forecast errors.
entries.note: 'Suspicious' strengthens the source's 'weirder' into a more specific insinuation.

entries.test: Successive financial disclosures for the discussed AI labs would show whether their aggregate costs declined during the period under discussion.
entries.note: The surrounding financial discussion supplies aggregate spending as the plain reading, rather than per-token prices.
'It appears' qualifies the allegation of deliberate concealment.
The graphic's labeling is publicly checkable; the full proposition additionally asserts its designers' private purpose.
Capability statements can be compared with performance, but the proposition also asserts Amodei's motive for making them.

entries.test: If the stated contractor-wide ban is enforced, subsequent evidence of Anthropic's business failure or sustained continued operation would test the predicted collapse.
entries.note: The antecedent is the broad commercial ban, not merely exclusion from government contracts.
The proposition removes 'I don't think.' It asserts an internal attitude and supports it with a counterfactual.
'Appears' qualifies the exclusivity claim; identifying the model as Claude reasonably resolves the source's wording.
The source limits its causal speculation to 'many' demands; the proposition generalizes it. Both the usage and causal claims are explicitly speculative.

entries.test: Dated versions of Anthropic's safety policy and contemporaneous profiles of Amodei would establish the pledge's wording, its removal, and the elapsed time.
entries.note: The original specifies an advance guarantee that safety measures were accurate, which the normalization changes to generic 'guaranteed safety measures.'
This is an ethical judgment. 'Like any other tech company' adds a universal comparison absent from 'the same old shit.'
He describes what the administration 'could' do, not what it will do if the condition arises.
'Far more likely' is an explicit comparative probability judgment.

entries.test: Documented evaluations or demonstrations of Claude performing bulk domestic surveillance and controlling fully autonomous weapons would test the asserted capability limits.
entries.note: These capability judgments are Zitron's parenthetical assertions, not the Atlantic quotation that follows.

entries.test: Publicly documented offers, proposals, or agreements by Anthropic to help the Pentagon improve autonomous weapons' accuracy would establish the stated willingness.
entries.note: The surrounding passage grounds 'wants to help' in a concrete reported offer, not solely an inaccessible preference.

entries.test: LLM reliability evaluations and Anthropic's published military-use terms would test unavoidable hallucination risk and the scope of permitted uses.
entries.note: The normalization drops the US-military scope and the surrounding restriction to lawful uses.
The source alleges concealment as the sole purpose and pleasing users as the chatbot's specific purpose; the normalization weakens both. The concealment motive is private.

entries.test: OpenAI's military contracts, payment terms, and Altman's public endorsement of those arrangements would establish his expressed willingness to earn revenue from military work.
entries.note: The normalized commercial assertion is factual, but it omits the quoted assertion that Altman 'loves war.'

entries.test: The amendment's signing history and published terms, interpreted alongside applicable surveillance law, would establish its status at publication and whether it permits domestic surveillance.
entries.note: The next sentence supplies the domestic-surveillance meaning of the alleged loopholes.

entries.test: The revised contract's enforceable surveillance restrictions and OpenAI's public descriptions of the agreement would establish the claimed latitude and comparison with Anthropic's requested terms.
entries.note: The source says the announcement enables a pretense; the proposition says OpenAI actually makes the claim.
The assertion concerns the private reputational purpose of the announcement.
This prescribes how readers should regard the two executives.
The proposition omits 'able' and changes apparent acceptance of harms into emotional unconcern. Their private degree of concern cannot be settled from their contracts alone.
The controlling claim is that neither deserves credit; the commercial allegation supplies its justification.

entries.test: The companies' military contracts and public statements promoting military cooperation would establish active, publicly welcomed participation in US military operations.
entries.note: He explicitly says this is not an overstatement and supports it with public expressions of commitment.
The proposition removes 'seems' and 'I'd argue' and substitutes Anthropic for Amodei.
There is no shared test for the unqualified assertion that generative AI 'isn't intelligent.' Specific capability overstatements could be tested separately.
It asserts that military reliance would have been impossible in a counterfactual world without the alleged falsehoods.

entries.test: Public investigations of lethal military operations using LLMs could establish whether false capability claims directly caused reliance on the systems and resulting deaths.
entries.note: This is a firm prospective causal assertion with no deadline.

entries.test: Independent demonstrations of novel LLM-generated ideas, evaluations of noncoding reliability, and coding-service cost records would test the asserted limitations and subsidy requirement.
entries.note: The absolute inability to generate unique ideas has a plain empirical reading, despite the broader evaluative language.
The description of actual military usage is explicitly qualified by 'probably'; the capability statement is firmer.
This assigns moral responsibility and prescribes a duty for journalists.
